title: Payment fragmentation turns checkout into a time, liquidity, trust, and consumer-optionality system
source_unit: Stitch, How South Africans Shop in 2026: Consumer Payments Report
geography: South Africa; digitally active consumers and Stitch platform transaction data

denominator.unit: approximately surveyed South African consumers; digitally active and online transacting sample

payment_fragmentation.value: No single payment method dominates; wallets, BNPL, bank-linked rails, mobile money, and crypto coexist

wallet_speed.value: About 3 seconds median wallet transaction versus roughly 15–30 seconds for cards in the report's platform comparison

observations.method: Stitch consumer survey of approximately 3,000 people, supplemented by Stitch Q1 2026 platform transaction data; survey and platform denominators are distinct.
observations.uncertainty: The sample is digitally active and not a population-representative estimate of all South African consumers. Company platform data, self-report, and commercial framing limit generalization.
observations.subgroup: Online transactors; detailed demographic and payment-use differences require the full report tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: Trying a payment method does not establish repeated use, lower cost, greater safety, or improved household welfare.

observations.period: 2026; online shopping repertoire and cross-border platform exposure

denominator.unit: approximately surveyed South African consumers; digitally active and online transacting sample

online_shopping_frequency.unit: percent shopping online as much as or more than in-store

international_low_cost_platform_use.unit: percent shopping on Temu, Shein, or AliExpress

platform_repertoire.value: Consumer choice spans brand sites, retailers, marketplaces, and international low-cost platforms

observations.method: Survey questions on online/in-store balance, shopping destinations, and platform use.
observations.uncertainty: Reported percentages describe the digitally active sample and do not measure total retail market share, product quality, labor conditions, or household affordability.
observations.subgroup: Digitally active South African consumers; category and income differences are not assumed without tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad platform access may increase choice while also increasing exposure to fraud, delivery risk, data extraction, and local-retailer pressure.

observations.period: 2026; BNPL, liquidity management, and payday timing

denominator.unit: Credit-active consumers for BNPL estimate; Stitch platform transaction data for shopping rhythm; no single pooled denominator

credit_active_bnpl_use.unit: percent of credit-active consumers using buy-now-pay-later

bnpl_omnichannel_preference.unit: percent wanting BNPL online and in-store

payday_basket_change.unit: percent increase in basket size around payday in Stitch platform data

monthly_volume_last_week.unit: percent of monthly transaction volume occurring in the last week

liquidity_mechanism.value: BNPL and payment timing operate as cash-flow management and access infrastructure, not only as discount or convenience features

observations.method: Stitch survey and Q1 2026 platform transaction analysis; the report separates credit-active consumer responses from platform timing patterns.
observations.uncertainty: BNPL use does not reveal repayment success, fees, distress, exclusion, or whether a purchase was necessary. Platform timing patterns are not population-level income-cycle estimates.
observations.subgroup: Credit-active consumers and Stitch platform users; the report identifies liquidity-management and no-funds buyer profiles but does not establish causal welfare effects.
observations.counterinterpretation: Payment flexibility can preserve participation while increasing repayment exposure or shifting rather than solving affordability pressure.

observations.period: 2026; payment failure, AI-mediated discovery, and agentic-commerce boundary

denominator.unit: Stitch platform transaction data and survey of digitally active consumers; no single pooled denominator

card_attempt_noncompletion.value: Nearly one in four card attempts did not complete on the Stitch platform in the report's Q1 comparison

failed_card_attempt_reason_invalid_detai.unit: percent of non-successful attempts attributed to invalid details

chatgpt_product_research.value: 31–34% of active ChatGPT users reported using it for product research or price comparison

agentic_boundary.value: Discovery and recommendation can move into AI interfaces before merchant checkout, payment authentication, fraud controls, and APIs are interoperable

observations.method: Stitch platform transaction data and survey responses, with the report distinguishing checkout performance from AI-use responses.
observations.uncertainty: The failure and AI measures are proprietary or self-reported, use different denominators, and do not establish lost sales, consumer harm, or an inevitable shift to agentic purchasing.
observations.subgroup: Stitch platform users and active ChatGPT users in the surveyed digital-consumer sample.
observations.counterinterpretation: Payment failure can reflect merchant, issuer, authentication, data-entry, or consumer factors; AI research use need not become AI-directed purchase execution.

related_sources.claim: Stitch companion article describes the approximately 3,000-person survey, 27 interviews, platform data, payment fragmentation, BNPL, checkout friction, and AI-shopping findings.

boundary: This is sponsor-produced commercial trend intelligence, not a nationally representative population survey or independent causal evaluation. It is useful for identifying mechanisms at the intersection of consumer culture, payment infrastructure, liquidity, time, trust, and AI-mediated commerce; it does not establish national prevalence, realized welfare, repayment outcomes, market share, or causal effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Stitch 2026 consumer-report landing page, checked against the publisher's companion methodology article.
reproduction_audit.version_note: The landing page is an interactive publisher report page. Survey, interview, and platform-data denominators must remain separate; platform findings should not be generalized to all South African commerce without independent validation.
